subject.title: fix(codex): bound app-server websocket handshake waits to requestTimeoutMs

question: Should Codex WebSocket and Unix upgrade handshakes use appServer.requestTimeoutMs as their fail-closed ceiling, and should this work proceed through this PR or the cleaner parallel PR?
rationale: The timeout fixes an indefinite hang but intentionally terminates legitimate slow upgrades, while two near-identical branches now compete and this one includes an unrelated security-boundary exception.

options.title: Use one Codex-only PR
options.body: Approve requestTimeoutMs as the shared handshake ceiling, select the branch without the unrelated APNs diff, and close the duplicate after confirming equivalent TCP and Unix coverage.

options.title: Keep this combined branch
options.body: Proceed with this PR only after explicitly approving the APNs boundary exception and confirming it belongs in the same landing unit.

options.title: Require a separate timeout policy
options.body: Pause both PRs and design a distinct handshake configuration surface, accepting additional config and upgrade complexity.

recommendation.title: Use one Codex-only PR
recommendation.body: Approve requestTimeoutMs as the shared handshake ceiling, select the branch without the unrelated APNs diff, and close the duplicate after confirming equivalent TCP and Unix coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The affected app-server transport ownership boundary appears to originate in steipete's merged Codex extension refactor.
